- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if spike > +10% from recent mean.
- If model forecast shows sharp upward spike (e.g. >+15% from 14-day mean) followed by 3+ consecutive days of downward trend, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g. >0.15 for 5+ days), model often overestimates; apply downward bias of 3–7% to forecast mean.
- Model tends to lag in early days of downturns; if true outcome drops >5% from 7-day mean, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead by -2–5% to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g. +0.17, -0.28, +0.17), model often misreads momentum; reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting sentiment noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply 3–5% downward adjustment to first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
